semantics: V1 ETL variants include TerraBase, SQL, OLAP, Elasticsearch, Queue, Snowflake, EmbeddingsGeneration, and GenAi task types where the pinned source exposes them.
Each destination defines load, insert-only or delete behavior, schema or table mapping, batching, provider limits, connection validation, and test-script results.
Unsupported combinations, including sharded or encrypted-channel limitations, are explicit capability errors rather than accepted as no-op tasks.
public_contract.compatibility: All pinned V1 ETL types remain in scope; exact V2 provider set and adapter ownership are unresolved.

risk.description: Treating provider-specific delivery as one generic sink hides ordering, transaction, size, and failure differences.

v1_evidence.scope: src/TerraBase.Server/Documents/ETL/EtlProcess.cs (Load, ForceBatchRetry, EnterFallbackMode, UpdateEtlProcessState, RecordLoadError, RecordConfigurationError, RecordUnknownError, GetPerformanceStats, and GetConnectionStatus), EtlProcessHealthStatus.cs, EtlProcessStatistics.cs, ETL/Handlers/Processors/AbstractEtlHandlerProcessorForRetryBatch.cs and task-error processors; test/TerraBase.SlowTests/Server/Documents/ETL/SQL/SqlEtlTests.cs, Elasticsearch/ElasticSearchEtlTests.cs, Queue/TerraBase_21530.cs, and EtlTasksManagement_TerraBase_7276.cs

semantics: ETL delivery reports running, disabled, fallback, healthy, impaired, failed, and stopped states with last successful batch and error details.
Batch retry, task error listing and deletion, dead-letter or equivalent failed-item handling, and reset behavior are explicit operations with bounded retries and durable checkpoints.
Progress, throughput, transformation, load, and resource metrics are stable typed records and never include connection credentials or customer payloads.
public_contract.compatibility: V1 ETL retry and observability behavior is unresolved pending fault-injection and metrics-shape tests.

risk.description: Retrying a failed external batch without a durable idempotency key can create duplicate side effects or mask a dead-letter backlog.

v1_evidence.scope: src/TerraBase.Client/Documents/Operations/ETL/Queue/QueueEtlConfiguration.cs, QueueConnectionString.cs, QueueBrokerType.cs, and provider connection settings for Amazon SQS, Azure Queue Storage, Azure Service Bus, Kafka, and RabbitMQ; src/TerraBase.Server/Documents/ETL/Providers/Queue/QueueEtl.cs, Kafka/KafkaEtl.cs, RabbitMq/RabbitMqEtl.cs, AmazonSqs/AmazonSqsEtl.cs, AzureQueueStorage/AzureQueueStorageEtl.cs, and CloudEventConverter.cs; test/TerraBase.SlowTests/Server/Documents/ETL/Queue

semantics: Queue ETL publishes transformed records as provider-specific messages, including CloudEvent metadata, headers or attributes, queue declarations, routing, FIFO and size constraints where supported.
Provider delivery errors, retries, delete-processed behavior, connection validation, and sharding limitations are observable and do not advance source checkpoints before a confirmed publish.
Connection strings are references to typed secret-bearing configuration, never values copied into logs, audit output, or parity evidence.
public_contract.compatibility: V1 queue ETL provider behavior is unresolved pending provider fixtures and failure/retry tests.

risk.description: A publish acknowledgment mismatch can lose records or duplicate messages in an external queue.

v1_evidence.scope: src/TerraBase.Client/Documents/Operations/QueueSink/QueueSinkConfiguration.cs, QueueSinkScript.cs, AddQueueSinkOperation.cs, and UpdateQueueSinkOperation.cs; src/TerraBase.Server/Documents/QueueSink/QueueSinkLoader.cs, QueueSinkProcess.cs, Test/TestQueueSinkScript.cs, ServerWide/Commands/QueueSink/AddQueueSinkCommand.cs and UpdateQueueSinkCommand.cs; test/TerraBase.SlowTests/Server/Documents/QueueSink/QueueSinkTestBase.cs, KafkaQueueSinkTests.cs, RabbitMqSinkTests.cs, AzureServiceBusSinkTests.cs, and Issues/TerraBase_22105.cs

semantics: Queue sinks validate task name, broker type, connection-string reference, non-empty unique scripts, disabled state, mentor and pinning, and provider-specific queue entries.
The process consumes messages, executes bounded scripts, writes documents or other supported records, and reports duplicate, parse, poison-message, and connection outcomes.
Changing a referenced connection or configuration restarts the correct process and preserves or resets its checkpoint according to an explicit V1-compatible rule.
public_contract.compatibility: V1 queue-sink behavior is unresolved pending typed adapter, process, and restart tests.

risk.description: A sink that acknowledges a message before its database write commits can lose source queue data.

v1_evidence.scope: src/TerraBase.Server/Documents/QueueSink/KafkaQueueSink.cs, RabbitMqQueueSink.cs, AzureServiceBusQueueSink.cs, QueueSinkProcess.cs, and QueueSinkLoader.cs; src/TerraBase.Client/Documents/Operations/QueueSink/AzureServiceBusSinkSource.cs; test/TerraBase.EndToEndTests/Server/Documents/QueueSink/AzureServiceBusSinkSourceTests.cs and test/TerraBase.SlowTests/Server/Documents/QueueSink/AzureServiceBusSinkTests.cs, KafkaQueueSinkTests.cs, RabbitMqSinkTests.cs, AzureServiceBusClusterSinkTests.cs

semantics: Kafka, RabbitMQ, and Azure Service Bus sinks preserve broker-specific queue, topic, subscription, routing, header, and acknowledgment rules.
Malformed queue or subscription entries fail validation; consumer errors enter a defined retry, fallback, poison-message or dead-letter state without acknowledging bad data.
Cluster responsibility transfer keeps one active sink owner, resumes from a durable checkpoint, and exposes failover and connection status to operations.
public_contract.compatibility: V1 broker-specific semantics are unresolved pending provider and cluster-failover tests; no generic broker abstraction is assumed.

risk.description: Broker acknowledgment and failover differences are exactly where duplicate or lost messages tend to hide.

v1_evidence.scope: src/TerraBase.Client/Documents/Operations/ConnectionStrings/ConnectionString.cs, GetConnectionStringsOperation.cs, PutConnectionStringOperation.cs, RemoveConnectionStringOperation.cs, ETL provider connection-string classes, and Queue/QueueConnectionString.cs; test/TerraBase.SlowTests/Server/Documents/ETL/ConnectionStringTests.cs and Snowflake/SnowflakeEtlTests.cs (audit JSON credential checks)

semantics: Connection strings are typed records with provider validation, get, put, remove, dependency checks, and stable names used by ETL and queue-sink tasks.
Audit and status serialization omits credentials, keys, tokens, and private connection details while retaining enough non-secret identity to diagnose a task.
The Platform Adapter enforces tenant authorization, audit, confirmation where required, and secret handling; the engine does not expose raw or generic HTTP access.
public_contract.compatibility: V1 typed connection-string behavior is unresolved pending authorization, dependency, and secret-redaction tests.

risk.description: Leaking a provider credential through status, audit, or parity evidence is a direct tenant-security failure.

items.name: ongoing-transfer-task-controls

v1_evidence.scope: src/TerraBase.Client/Documents/Operations/OngoingTasks/GetOngoingTaskInfoOperation.cs, ToggleOngoingTaskStateOperation.cs, DeleteOngoingTaskOperation.cs, and OngoingTask types; src/TerraBase.Server/Documents/OngoingTasks/AbstractOngoingTasks.cs, OngoingTasks.cs, Commands/OngoingTasks/GetOngoingTasksCommand.cs, and Dashboard/Cluster/Notifications/OngoingTasksNotificationSender.cs; test/TerraBase.RachisTests/DatabaseCluster/OngoingTasks.cs, test/TerraBase.SlowTests/Server/Documents/OngoingTasks/PinOnGoingTaskToMentorNode.cs, and ETL task-management tests

semantics: Operations list, inspect, disable, enable, and delete transfer tasks by stable ID or name and report task type, responsible member, state, connection status, progress, and error details.
The task inventory includes periodic backup, subscriptions, ETL variants, queue sinks, and other transfer-owned operations while retaining a clear distinction from private control-plane tasks.
Mutations use the typed authorized seam, are concurrency-safe, audit their result, and never turn task inspection into a generic route or secret-read capability.
public_contract.compatibility: V1 operational controls are unresolved pending typed adapter authorization and status-shape tests.

downstream_impact: backup, subscription, ETL, and queue-sink owners

risk.description: A task control race can stop the wrong owner, leave two workers active, or expose private control-plane state.

v1_evidence.scope: src/TerraBase.Server/Documents/Replication/BucketMigrationReplication.cs, Incoming/IncomingMigrationReplicationHandler.cs, Outgoing/OutgoingMigrationReplicationHandler.cs, Senders/MigrationReplicationDocumentSender.cs, ServerWide/Commands/Sharding/StartBucketMigrationCommand.cs and migration completion commands; test/TerraBase.RachisTests/DatabaseCluster/EtlFailover.cs, SubscriptionsFailover.cs, test/TerraBase.SlowTests/Sharding/ETL/ShardedEtlFailoverTests.cs, and Sharding/Subscriptions/SubscriptionsWithReshardingTests.cs

semantics: Transfer-owned consumers define what happens to subscription, ETL, queue-sink, and backup checkpoints during member loss, bucket migration, responsibility transfer, replay, and rejoin.
Replication owns core acknowledgement and convergence decisions; this row records only handoff obligations needed to prevent duplicate or lost transfer work.
Tenant isolation, source and destination identity, old-owner fencing, and recovery after interrupted migration require scenario tests and redacted Replication or Recovery Receipts.
No replication algorithm, consistency default, or conflict policy is selected by this unresolved contract row.
public_contract.compatibility: V1 failure-domain interactions are unresolved and require a separately accepted multi-region scenario contract.

risk.description: A transfer task that outlives its owner without fencing can write duplicates or continue against the wrong tenant or member.

v1_evidence.scope: src/TerraBase.Server/Documents/Sharding/Handlers/Processors/Streaming, Subscriptions, Smuggler, and OngoingTasks; src/TerraBase.Server/Documents/Sharding/Streaming/CombinedReadContinuationState.cs, CombinedStreamResult.cs, ReadContinuationState.cs, and Subscriptions/ShardedSubscriptionWorker.cs; src/TerraBase.Client/Documents/Operations/Backups/Sharding/ShardRestoreSettings.cs; test/TerraBase.SlowTests/Sharding/Backup/ShardedBackupTests.cs, ShardedRestoreBackupTests.cs, ShardedSmugglerTests.cs, ETL/ShardedEtlTests.cs, Subscriptions/ShardedSubscriptionClusterTests.cs, ShardedSubscriptionConcurrentTests.cs, and ShardedSubscriptionSlowTests.cs

semantics: Sharded streaming, subscription, Smuggler, backup, restore, and ETL operations identify shard ownership and preserve per-shard checkpoint, ordering, and failure semantics.
Merged results define continuation state, duplicate behavior, shard failure, partial completion, and rejoin instead of presenting an unordered aggregate as complete.
Shard restore settings and migration controls remain typed and tenant-scoped; they do not grant direct access to private shard or control-plane routes.
public_contract.compatibility: V1 sharded transfer behavior is unresolved pending per-shard and aggregate qualification tests.

risk.description: A merged continuation that advances one shard but loses another can create an apparently complete but incomplete transfer.

v1_evidence.scope: src/TerraBase.Client/Documents/Smuggler/SmugglerProgressBase.cs, SmugglerResult.cs, OfflineMigrationProgress.cs, OfflineMigrationResult.cs, Backups/BackupProgress.cs, BackupResult.cs, PeriodicBackupStatus.cs, ETL/EtlProcessState.cs, and QueueSink/QueueSinkProcessState.cs; src/TerraBase.Server/Documents/ETL/Stats, QueueSink/Stats, PeriodicBackup/Progress.cs, and Dashboard/DatabasesOngoingTasksInfo.cs; src/TerraBase.Server/Documents/Commands/ETL and OngoingTasks; test/TerraBase.SlowTests/Server/Documents/ETL and PeriodicBackup status and progress tests

semantics: Progress and status records identify the operation and non-secret counts, rates, checkpoints, current step, health, responsible member, and terminal error without exposing payloads or credentials.
Reads and mutations are separate typed operations; retrying a status read is safe, while a mutation requires V1 authorization, confirmation, idempotency, and audit rules.
Metrics distinguish source extraction, transformation, destination delivery, backup upload, restore, and skipped or dead-letter records so a green status cannot hide loss.
public_contract.compatibility: V1 status and metrics shapes are unresolved pending protocol snapshots, secret scans, and failure-path tests.

risk.description: A misleading green status is operationally worse than a visible failure because it prevents recovery action.

v1_evidence.scope: src/TerraBase.Server/Smuggler/Documents/Actions/DatabaseRecordActions.cs permission-gated imports, src/TerraBase.Server/Documents/Handlers/Processors/Smuggler, OngoingTasks, ETL, and Subscriptions, client operation classes for typed requests, and audit serializers in backup, ETL, queue-sink, and connection-string configuration; test/TerraBase.SlowTests/Server/Documents/ETL/ConnectionStringTests.cs and authorization-sensitive Smuggler tests

semantics: Every transfer operation states actor authorization, tenant and database scope, confirmation requirements, audit event, secret handling, and typed error behavior.
Permission-denied configuration records are reported as skipped or failed according to V1 behavior and never become an implicit success or authorization bypass.
Private control-plane routes, raw engine access, and generic HTTP escape hatches are outside this public seam even when V1 has internal handlers with similar names.
public_contract.compatibility: Platform and private-route classification is explicitly unresolved until the approved typed adapter and security tests settle the public contract; no transfer feature is excluded.

risk.description: Confusing an internal administrative handler with a public engine operation can expose cross-tenant data or credentials.
